draft_key_information_units.information: Eleving Group achieved record-high revenue of EUR 250.0 million in 2025, representing a 15.5% year-on-year increase, with EBITDA reaching EUR 101.9 million (13.5% increase) and net profit stable at EUR 29.2 million. The net portfolio grew 20.2% to EUR 446.3 million.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management Report '2025 at a glance'; Consolidated Statement of Profit and Loss and Other Comprehensive Income

draft_key_information_units.information: Revenue breakdown shows traditional vehicle financing decreased 6.0% to EUR 67.0 million, flexible vehicle financing increased 25.9% to EUR 60.3 million, device financing contributed EUR 7.9 million (launched in 2025), and consumer lending grew 18.0% to EUR 114.8 million.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Keynote from the CEO section detailing business line contributions

draft_key_information_units.information: Strategic expansions included launching installment loans in European markets (Latvia, Estonia, Romania, Armenia), introducing smartphone financing in Kenya and Uganda (portfolio EUR 13.5 million by year-end), entering Tanzania as a new market, and piloting AI voice agents at call centers.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management Report sections on Operations in European/African markets, Outlook, and Operational efficiency

draft_key_information_units.information: Capital management involved completing a EUR 40 million bond tap in March 2025 and refinancing/new bond issuances of EUR 275 million in October 2025. Dividends of EUR 19.65 million were distributed, representing a 10% cash yield based on IPO price.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management Report Capital management section; Consolidated Statement of Cash Flows

draft_key_information_units.information: Impairment expense increased to EUR 54.2 million in 2025, driven by formal derecognition of long-overdue balances deemed unrecoverable, which triggered a corresponding reversal of accumulated impairment allowances.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Note 7: Impairment expense section; Consolidated Statement of Profit and Loss

draft_key_information_units.information: A regulatory decision in Moldova alleged non-compliance with consumer credit legislation regarding daily fees and total loan costs for approximately 1,080 contracts; the subsidiary is challenging the decision through administrative and judicial proceedings.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management Report Regulatory matter in Moldova section

draft_key_information_units.information: Post-reporting-period events include ongoing monitoring of Middle East conflict with no direct financial impact, and attraction of approximately EUR 12.3 million in additional funding from P2P platforms plus increased local borrowings in Kenya of EUR 6.3 million.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management Report Events after balance sheet date section

evaluation.selection_rationale: Prioritized headline financial performance (D1), major business line revenue changes (D2), strategic expansions and product launches (D3), capital structure and dividend actions (D4), significant impairment movements (D5), material regulatory exposure (D6), and relevant post-period events affecting liquidity (D7). Units represent independently omittable material themes directly supported by source evidence, aligning with instructions to emphasize performance drivers, segment developments, liquidity/financing, and strategic actions while excluding routine boilerplate.
